summary: Submission approvable with 1 minor warning(s) — file a corrections record on merge

findings.message: Source fetched via Archive.org fallback (original returned 200)
Misattributed statistic: 13.6% figure mischaracterized as cloud-hosted-specific and as independently confirmed by The Register
findings.details: Article states: 'Huntress reported that about 13.6 percent of reachable cloud-hosted servers remained unpatched, while 28.6 percent of reachable self-hosted N-central servers were still unpatched — a figure The Register independently reported as well.' The Huntress snapshot (source-1.html.gz) actually says: 'Overall, we see about 13.6% reachable servers overall are still unpatched (including both cloud and self-hosted reachable servers). Notably, the majority of the remaining unpatched servers are self-hosted: 28.6% of the reachable N-central self-hosted servers are still unpatched.' The 13.6% figure is the combined cloud+self-hosted total, not a cloud-hosted-specific figure. Additionally, The Register snapshot (source-2.html.gz) does not report a 13.6% figure at all — it only states 'nearly all cloud-hosted N-central instances had been patched' (qualitative, no percentage) alongside the 28.6% self-hosted figure. The claim that The Register 'independently reported' the 13.6% figure is not supported by the source.

content_preview.title: CISA Orders Federal Agencies to Patch Actively Exploited N-able N-central Authentication Bypass
content_preview.summary: CISA gave federal agencies until August 6 to patch CVE-2026-18577, an N-central auth bypass exploited in the wild since July 31 that grants attackers admin access to the RMM console.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added an N-able N-central authentication-bypass flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 3, 2026, giving federal civilian agencies until [August 6 to remediate](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json). N-able disclosed the vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-18577, on [August 2](https://status.n-able.com/2026/08/02/n-central-2026-3-hotfix-1-mitigation-for-cve-2026-18...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News-category piece with clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure, appropriate for a developing vulnerability story. Word count (537) is within the News range (400-1200).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 7 source snapshots from sources/2026-08/cisa-orders-federal-agencies-to-patch-actively-exploited-n-able-n-central-authentication-bypass/ (decompressed via gunzip, cross-checked against manifest.json sha256 filenames — no re-fetching of live URLs was needed). source-0 (thehackernews.com): confirms CVSS 8.2, incomplete-patch relationship to CVE-2026-18556, Aug 6 FCEB deadline, svchost.exe/Cloudflared IOCs, attacker IPs. source-1 (huntress.com): confirms verbatim 'god-mode' quote, Take Control abuse, Cloudflare tunnel persistence, IOC IPs/domains — but the article's characterization of the 13.6% statistic does not match this source (see finding above). source-2 (theregister.com): confirms 'full administrative access to an N-central console' framing, CVSS 8.2 (CVSSv4), NHS England and Belgium CCB advisories, CVE-2026-18556→2026.2 patch/exploitation-route history, BOD 26-04 three-day deadline mechanism — but does NOT independently report a 13.6% figure (only 'nearly all cloud-hosted instances patched', qualitative). source-3 (cisa.gov KEV JSON): confirms dateAdded 2026-08-03, dueDate 2026-08-06, knownRansomwareCampaignUse 'Unknown', BOD 26-04 requiredAction text, CVE-2026-18556 incomplete-patch description verbatim. Note: the KEV JSON schema has no CVSS field at all (checked keys across the full 1660-entry catalog) — the article's sentence attributing an '8.2' CVSS score jointly to CISA, The Hacker News and The Register slightly overstates CISA's role as a CVSS source, though the underlying 8.2 figure itself is accurate per NVD/CNA data and both news outlets. Minor, not corrections-worthy on its own. source-4 (nvd.nist.gov): confirms 'Versions through 2026.3.1' affected language matching the article's 'all N-central versions through 2026.3.1', CVSS-BT 8.2 from N-able as CNA. source-5 (n-able.com blog, Archive.org fallback — live URL also returned 200 per manifest, but snapshot used the archived version per policy): confirms verbatim 'A limited number of customers have been identified to be impacted by this, and, for those impacted customers, N-able support has directly engaged,' Cloudflare tunnel persistence, background timeline (July 31 licensing anomalies -> Aug 2 hotfix). source-6 (status.n-able.com): confirms hotfix build 2026.3.1.7, NCOD automatic upgrade vs. self-hosted manual upgrade, svchost.exe/Cloudflared IOC list matching Huntress. No suspicious_patterns flagged in manifest.json for any of the 7 sources (all null) — no prompt-injection concerns found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: One recoverable inaccuracy found: the article states 13.6% is a cloud-hosted-specific unpatched rate 'independently reported' by The Register, but Huntress's own text defines 13.6% as the combined cloud+self-hosted overall rate, and The Register does not report that number at all (only a qualitative 'nearly all cloud-hosted instances patched'). This is a single subordinate statistic in the body, not the headline/summary/lead, and does not affect the article's central thesis (CISA ordering federal patching of an actively exploited N-central auth bypass). All other specifics — CVE numbers, CVSS score, dates, hotfix build, IOCs, quotes, NHS/Belgium advisories — verified against source text.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference, appropriate hedging in 'What We Don't Know' section.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/ (including the 2026-08/ monthly folder) and all 2026-08 submissions for existing N-able/N-central/CVE-2026-1857x coverage — none found. This is genuinely the first submission on this story; it is the lowest-numbered of six open PRs (#2128, #2129, #2131, #2133, #2135, #2136) covering the same CISA KEV listing, but since none of the other five have merged, no duplicate exists in the archive at review time. Reviewed strictly on its own merits per editorial policy.
concerns: 13.6% statistic is mischaracterized as a cloud-hosted-specific figure independently confirmed by The Register, when Huntress's source text defines it as the combined overall (cloud+self-hosted) rate and The Register does not report a 13.6% figure at all.

huntress.com, n-able.com, and status.n-able.com are not yet on config/source_allowlist.txt, though all three are legitimate primary/vendor sources directly analogous to already-allowlisted cybersecurity vendor blogs (e.g. tenable.com, rapid7.com, securitylabs.datadoghq.com) and the vendor's own advisory/status page for a vulnerability in its own product.
recommendations: File a corrections record clarifying that Huntress's 13.6% figure is the combined cloud+self-hosted unpatched rate, not a cloud-hosted-specific rate, and that The Register did not independently report that number.
Consider adding huntress.com, n-able.com, and status.n-able.com to config/source_allowlist.txt given they are reputable, directly-relevant primary sources used appropriately here.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively solid, well-sourced spot-news coverage of a real CISA KEV listing with an actively exploited RMM auth-bypass vulnerability. All central claims (CVE identity, CVSS severity, CISA deadline, exploitation timeline, IOCs, vendor quotes) verified against source snapshots. One recoverable statistical misattribution in a body paragraph warrants a corrections note; it does not touch the headline, summary, or lead. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
